name: Mucomuscular flap lip augmentation

card.summary: Surgical lip enlargement by moving intraoral tissue into the lip; the only source reviewed describes flaps generally as adding little volume.
card.note: Very thin sourcing: no studies specific to this technique were found.

quick.overview:
Surgical flap procedures move small strips of tissue from near the lips or inside the mouth into the lip. Wikipedia says this adds little volume and gives only slight protrusion.

No studies specific to mucomuscular flap augmentation were found, and the registered trials surfaced under this name concern dental implants and bone grafting.
quick.mechanism: A strip of mucosa and underlying muscle is repositioned within the lip to increase bulk.
quick.risks: General lip surgery risks listed on Wikipedia include bleeding, swelling, uneven lips and lumpiness; no figures for this technique were found.

lead: Mucomuscular flap lip augmentation refers to surgical lip enlargement using tissue from inside the mouth. Wikipedia describes lip augmentation by flaps, in which small strips of skin from near the lips or inside the mouth are moved to the lips, and says this adds little volume and produces only slight protrusion [1].
No clinical studies specific to this technique were found, so this entry is brief.

paras: Flap techniques differ from implants and fillers in using the patient's own nearby tissue [1].
